2026-11-v2.heading: What the QR code does
2026-11-v2.asked: The doctor is asked, for each pattern on the note, whether it was a prescribing cascade and what was done (for example dose changed, or no change).
2026-11-v2.stored: Janus stores only the doctor's answers, the week of the answer, the region of the note, and for each answered pattern its rule, the codes of its two medicines and of the event, the direction (unwanted or improvement) and whether the product was confirmed. No names, no box names and no dates finer than a week. The medicine list itself is not stored.
2026-11-v2.howLong: The link works for about five weeks. Answers are kept for at most 24 months and are shown only as counts for groups of at least 20 answers, with noise added.
2026-11-v2.withdraw: You can withdraw at any time with the token kept on this device: the doctor can then no longer answer, and answers already sent are deleted.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.intro: Janus is a research prototype, not a medical device. This page says what stays on your device, what is sent, what is stored, for how long, and how to delete it.

device.title: What stays on this device
device.body: Photos of boxes and labels, the recognised text, your medicine list with the names on the boxes and, for a scanned box, its lot number, your settings, the tokens of the outcome loop and of donations, and reminders. They live only in this browser; Janus has no account.

sent.title: What is sent to Janus
sent.body: Product codes (only the GTIN, the expiry and the national product number of a pack code; never its serial or lot number), NDCs, the words you type or choose for a search, the ids of the medicines you confirmed with their start months, and the choices you make. Not the photos, not the recognised text as a whole and not the names on the boxes. Requests are not stored.

stored.title: What is stored
stored.body: Only if you choose: a donated report (age band, optional sex, region, medicines, event, kind, week, consent version), and the doctor's answers to a note's QR code. Janus also keeps a code of used or withdrawn notes until they expire, so a link cannot be used twice.

where.title: Where donated data are stored

howLong.title: For how long
howLong.body: Donated reports and doctors' answers: at most 24 months. Outcome-loop links: about five weeks (28 to 35 days).

delete.title: How to delete
delete.body: A donation: with its deletion token. Outcome-loop data: withdraw with the note's token. Everything on this device: Settings › Delete everything on this device.

protection.title: How shared numbers are protected, and the limits
protection.body: Counts from donations and doctors' answers are shown only for groups of at least 20, with random noise added (Hidden under 20, noise added). This is not formal differential privacy for the release as a whole.
protection.limits: Known limits: comparing a set of counts in two steps, (A) − (A,B) − (A,C) + (A,B,C), is not covered. Until rate limits exist (Phase 5), someone who can add donations can pad a group and re-draw its noise; anyone can create note tokens and report outcomes, so a group of doctors' answers can be padded in the same way.

legal.title: Legal frame
legal.body: In the EU, donations rely on explicit consent under the GDPR; in Türkiye, on explicit consent under the KVKK. In the US, Janus is not a HIPAA covered entity and follows the strictest of these rule sets. No outside body has audited Janus, and Janus is not a medical device.

network.title: Network provider
network.body: Janus is delivered through Cloudflare, which carries the encrypted connection between your browser and the Janus server and blocks attacks. To do this, Cloudflare processes technical data of each request, such as your IP address, browser type and time, and may set a short-lived technical cookie that tells people apart from automated traffic. Janus adds no analytics, no advertising and no tracking cookies, and its own server does not record IP addresses.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.body: openFDA (NDC Directory and FAERS / FDA AEMS), TİTCK (Türkiye), BDPM (France), CIMA by AEMPS (Spain), Wikidata, the PIPC list of prescribing cascades, Crossref and Retraction Watch for retraction checks, and MedDRA terms in report statistics (MedDRA® trademark is registered by IFPMA on behalf of ICH). Each result shows its source and date; none of these publishers endorses Janus.

codes.spontaneous_reporting: Reports are sent voluntarily and are not verified.
codes.not_incidence: The counts do not show how often an event happens.
codes.deduplicated_by_case_version_only: Only repeated versions of the same case are merged, so one event can still appear in more than one case.
codes.window_includes_follow_ups: Counts cover reports received or updated in the four quarters {first}–{last}, including follow-up versions of cases first received earlier.
codes.denominator_mapped_reports: Counts use only reports that name at least one medicine Janus recognizes ({share} of the reports in this window). Some spellings are not recognized, so a pattern can be missed. Figures for all reports are shown beside these.
codes.region_is_report_origin: A report's region is the country where the event is said to have happened or, when that is missing, where the reporter is. It does not tell where the medicine was taken or where it was bought.
codes.eu_member_states_not_separable: EU means the 27 member states pooled; FAERS cannot tell them apart.
codes.regions_not_comparable: Regions are not comparable as rates, because reporting habits differ. A different label in two regions can come from different numbers of reports, not from a different pattern. Each region is compared only with the other reports from the same region.
codes.absence_is_not_reassurance: No reports, or a pattern that is not clear, does not mean there is no association or that your medicines are free of problems.
codes.counts_built_against_other_dataset: These counts were built with a different version of the medicine name list than the one now in use.
codes.source_may_be_outdated: The FAERS data is older than expected for its update schedule.
codes.reported_together_only: These counts only show that the medicines appear together in reports.
codes.no_reports: No reports were found in this window.
codes.insufficient_data: Too few reports to show a pattern (fewer than 3).
codes.not_disproportionate: The event does not appear in a clearly larger share of the reports that name this medicine. This does not mean there is no association.
codes.weak: Few reports; treat as a weak pattern.
codes.weak_pattern: Few reports; treat as a weak pattern.
codes.disproportionate: The event appears in a larger share of the reports that name this medicine than in the other reports that name a recognized medicine.
codes.estimate_uses_continuity_correction: The size of this ratio depends on a small adjustment made because a count is zero.
codes.interval_approximate: The range is approximate and is less reliable when few reports are involved.
codes.denominator_sensitive: The result changes when all reports are used as the comparison.
codes.combination_caveat: These counts are for reports that name all of these medicines. The comparison group is every other report, including reports that name only some of them, so a pattern here may come from just one of the medicines. It does not show that taking them together has an effect.
codes.set_counts_are_lower_bounds: Counts for a set of medicines are lower bounds: a report counts only if every medicine in it was recognized.
codes.below_display_threshold: Too few reports name all of these medicines, so smaller groups are shown.
codes.single_shown: Showing each medicine on its own.
codes.event_not_reported_in_window: This event was not reported in this window.
codes.benefit_not_in_faers: FAERS has no report type for improvements, so only Janus donated reports can show this.
codes.layer_unavailable: This layer is not available right now.
codes.memory_unavailable: Collective Memory data is not available right now.

Onset.intro: For each pattern of the PIPC list (drug A → event → drug B): how long after starting a medicine of drug A's class do FAERS reporters say the event began? A method based on the time machine's, with stricter rules, for all 65 rows, with the number of reports behind each figure.

caveats.title: Read these first
caveats.descriptive: Descriptive only. It does not show that a medicine caused the event.
caveats.not_incidence: Not incidence: there is no count of people who took the medicine. One patient can appear in several reports.
caveats.selection: Only reports with a complete therapy start date and a complete event date have an interval. They may not represent all reports; long-standing use is dated less often, which can make intervals shorter.
caveats.zero_day: A 0-day interval often means one date was written in both fields; heaping at zero pulls the median down.
caveats.day_one: Dates on the 1st of a month (and on 1 January) are far more common than chance, often a filled-in day. A check without them is given; it is not a correction.
caveats.clusters: When one identical pair of dates holds more than a quarter of a row's reports, the row shows counts only.
caveats.small_sample: Below 10 reports with an interval: counts only. From 10 to 29: small sample; the estimates are unstable and the intervals may understate the uncertainty.
caveats.shared_rows: Rows with the same drug A class and event (they differ in drug B) have the same numbers.
caveats.receipt_window: Four quarters of reports by date received; event dates can be years earlier.
caveats.event_date_report_level: FAERS gives one event date per report: in a report with several events, the date may belong to another event than this row's.
caveats.median_interval: Use the exact interval of the median; the bootstrap interval in the downloads can understate the uncertainty on tied or small data.
caveats.shortest_interval: Per report, the interval starts at the most recently started medicine of the class; after a switch within the class it is shorter than the time since the class was first started (another reading is given).
caveats.class_membership: Drug A's class is matched on ingredient ATC codes; most local routes (skin, eye, airways…) are not counted and some ingredients are left out per class, with reasons in the dataset.
caveats.weibull: The Weibull shape reflects reporting artefacts as much as timing; it is not a mechanism, and it is published only with at least 30 reports.

statusLegend.title: What the status means
statusLegend.described: At least 30 reports with an interval: median, quartiles and the exact 95% interval of the median.
statusLegend.small_sample: 10 to 29 reports with an interval: median and intervals shown as a small sample; they are unstable.
statusLegend.cluster_dominated: One identical pair of dates holds more than a quarter of the reports (possible duplicates or a case series): counts only.
statusLegend.count_only: Fewer than 10 reports with an interval: counts only, no median.
statusLegend.no_interval: Reports exist, but none has a usable interval (the reasons are on the row). No timing can be described; this is not evidence of no effect.
statusLegend.no_candidate_reports: No report in the window names a medicine of this class as a suspect together with this event. This is not evidence of no effect.

Developers.title: For developers & clinicians
Developers.intro: Janus's checks and open datasets are available to other software: an MCP server for AI assistants, a CDS Hooks service for EHR sandboxes, a public read-only API and open data packages. All of it is open source.
Developers.notClinical: Research prototype, not a medical device and not for clinical use. Do not connect Janus to a live EHR.

mcp.title: MCP server for AI assistants
mcp.summary: Seven read-only tools over the Janus API
mcp.body: janus-mcp lets Claude, Kiro or any MCP client resolve a medicine, check a list for possible prescribing cascades and read the PIPC rows and the time machine. It is a thin client: every tool sends one request to the API and returns its answer unchanged. Set JANUS_API_URL to a local API or to this deployment's /api.
mcp.safety: Every result carries Janus's safety rules for the assistant: a finding is a possible pattern, never a verdict, and no advice to start, change or end a medicine.
mcp.privacy: The server logs nothing of a call and keeps nothing between calls. The medicines an assistant sends are seen by the assistant's provider.

cds.title: CDS Hooks service
cds.body: The service reads draft orders and prefetched medicines as FHIR R4, maps NDC, RxNorm and ATC codes through the Janus resolution layer and answers with information cards for possible prescribing cascades from the PIPC list. Nothing is stored.
cds.cards: Cards are always "info", with the PIPC row, the evidence and the disclaimer; no suggestions and no actions. No card does not mean the medicines are free of problems.

api.title: Public read-only API
api.summary: OpenAPI 3.1, no personal data in or out
api.body: The public routes take no request body and only read precomputed or released data: the onset table, the data-quality report, the cascade package, the open outcome dataset, the time machine and the CDS Hooks discovery.
api.rules: Errors are codes. Medical routes are not cached and log only route, status and latency. Counts are reports, never people.

server.limits: At most {slots} runs at a time and {queue} waiting; each run stops after {timeout} seconds; results are kept for {ttl} hours.
server.idle: Choose the inputs and start a run. The result appears here.
server.stoppedPolling: Still not finished. The page stopped asking; try again later.

form.title: Inputs
form.doseHelp: Within the fixed bounds of this model; a model input, not a dose for anyone.
form.outOfBounds: This value is outside the allowed bounds. Nothing is run until it is inside them.
form.noPerson: There is no entry for body weight, age, kidney function or any other personal detail: the model describes a virtual population only.
form.fix: Correct the highlighted input to see the result.
form.httkDose: httk runs use 1 mg per kg per day, as in the time machine, far above usual doses of these drugs: only the ratio between the two virtual populations is meaningful.
form.httkComparison: The run compares the two predefined HTTK-Pop virtual populations: adults aged 20–50 and adults aged 65–79.

populationBasis.amlodipine_adult: The cited parameters from 12 young healthy volunteers (Faulkner 1986) with the cited spreads; the clearance spread is a judgement that already covers the older-versus-younger difference.
populationBasis.amlodipine_adult_65plus: Clearance scaled by 19/25, the older-versus-younger amlodipine clearance of Abernethy 1990 (hypertensive patients, mean age 68), on top of the same spreads; the other parameters are unchanged. Ages 80 and over are not covered.
populationBasis.rhein_adult: The cited apparent parameters (Magnard 1993, healthy volunteers); bioavailability fixed at 1 because the parameters are already apparent. No data on older adults was verified, so no older-adult population is offered.

validation.title: How well the model matched published data for {compound}
validation.folds: Model peak {cmax}-fold {cdir} than published; area under the curve {auc}-fold {adir}.

meaning.credible: Within 2-fold of the published values for the checked scenario; still a model of a virtual population.
meaning.borderline: Between 2- and 3-fold: read the shape and the spread, not the absolute numbers.
meaning.failed: More than 3-fold apart: the absolute numbers are not validated; only relative comparisons are shown for research.

validation.aucNotIndependent: The published AUC shares a source with a model parameter, so only the peak comparison is an independent check.

scope.amlodipine: Checked against one 10 mg dose in healthy volunteers (Soria-Chacartegui 2023); other doses and schedules are not checked.
scope.rhein: Checked against one 38.58 mg dose (rhein equivalent, given as 50 mg diacerein) in healthy volunteers; other doses and schedules are not checked.
scope.httk: Checked against one oral dose per drug in healthy adults (time machine).

labelHalfLife.single: Half-life reported in the US label: {hours} h ({route}).

route.unknown: route not stated in the label sentence

labelHalfLife.context: A label value is a measurement quoted from the label; the model value is a prediction. Against a published reference set (Lombardo 2018), label half-lives were within 2-fold for {label}% of {n} drugs and httk half-lives for {httk}% of the same drugs. Extraction was automated; expert review has not yet been done. Shown for comparison only: it is not used in any simulation.

modelError.title: Measured model error
modelError.halfLife: Model half-life of the drug: {hours} h (calibrated 80% interval {low}–{high} h).
modelError.interval: Calibrated on Obach 2008, n = {n}; covers the true value about {nominal}% of the time in held-out drugs.
modelError.bias: Measured against Obach 2008 human data ({n} drugs, retrieved {date}): httk half-lives are {bias}-fold {direction} on geometric average; {within}% within 2-fold; geometric mean fold error {gmfe}.
modelError.notValidated: The steady-state concentrations are not validated against measured data; no calibrated interval exists for them.
modelError.compartmental: No calibrated interval: the bands show the spread of the virtual population, not the model's error. Concentrations, peaks and areas are not validated against measured data beyond the one study above.
